questions.q: Which compound undergoes the Cannizzaro reaction with concentrated NaOH?
questions.explain: (CH₃)₃CCHO has no α-hydrogen, so it disproportionates in concentrated base. Acetaldehyde and propanal have α-H and give aldol, and ketones do not give Cannizzaro.

questions.q: A mixture of benzaldehyde and formaldehyde is heated with concentrated NaOH. The main products are:
options: Benzyl alcohol and sodium benzoate only
questions.explain: In this crossed Cannizzaro reaction the more reactive HCHO is attacked by OH⁻ and oxidised to HCOONa, while benzaldehyde receives the hydride and is reduced to C₆H₅CH₂OH.

questions.q: 2-Methylpropanal is treated with dilute NaOH. Which statement about the product is correct?
options: It is 3-hydroxy-2,2,4-trimethylpentanal, which cannot dehydrate to an enone
It is 2,2,4-trimethylpent-2-enal formed by aldol condensation
It is a 1 : 1 mixture of 2-methylpropan-1-ol and sodium 2-methylpropanoate
No reaction occurs because the aldehyde has only one α-hydrogen
questions.explain: With one α-H, dilute base gives the aldol addition product, but its new α-carbon is quaternary with no H left, so dehydration is impossible. The alcohol plus carboxylate are the products in concentrated base.

questions.q: When the Cannizzaro reaction of benzaldehyde is carried out in D₂O with NaOD, the benzyl alcohol formed contains no deuterium on carbon. This shows that:
options: The reaction proceeds through an enolate intermediate
The solvent supplies the hydride that reduces the aldehyde
The rate-determining step is attack of OD⁻ on the carbonyl carbon
The hydrogen reaching the reduced aldehyde is transferred directly as hydride from another aldehyde molecule
questions.explain: If the solvent supplied the C–H hydrogen, deuterium would appear on carbon. Its absence shows hydride moves directly from the tetrahedral anion RCH(OH)O⁻ to a second aldehyde.
